title: Constructor or setter injection
context: Should you use constructor injection or setter injection?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Spring knowledge and questions
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Prefer constructor injection. Required dependencies are passed in once, the fields can be final, the object is never half-built, and tests can create it with plain code. A missing dependency fails at startup. Setter injection suits optional dependencies that have a sensible default. It can leave an object partly configured. Field injection with @Autowired is convenient but hides dependencies and makes tests harder.

points.title: Immutable, complete objects
points.why: Constructor injection allows final fields and guarantees all required dependencies exist.

points.title: Field injection drawbacks
points.why: Field injection hides dependencies and needs a container to test the class.
